title: AI Video Isn't the Problem. AI Slop Is.
topic: Why platforms are drawing a line between AI-assisted creation and repetitive AI spam
summary: A concise original explainer on why AI-assisted video can remain monetizable while repetitive spam, weak disclosure and copycat production create platform and audience risk.

sources.name: TikTok Newsroom - Helping people spot and understand AI generated content

creatorSignals: original distinction between AI as a tool and AI slop as an operating model
original monetization-oriented framework: authorship + transformation + disclosure

safety.notes: No creator clips, screenshots, logos, likenesses, copyrighted music, allegations or copied scripts. Claims are limited to official TikTok transparency/spam-detection policy and original analysis.

publish.title: AI Video Isn't the Problem. AI Slop Is. #Shorts
publish.caption:
AI-assisted creation can be powerful. The risk starts when automation turns into repetitive, interchangeable spam. TikTok says it is testing stronger detection for accounts dedicated to AI-generated spam. The durable model is AI + authorship: original thesis, real transformation, clear disclosure, and a visual identity that changes with the idea.
